The sutra translated this morning was commissioned by the Sagely, Divine, Martial, and Civil Emperor in the fourth year of the Zhenyuan era, the year of Wuchen (788 CE), by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Prajña of Kapiśā together with the Śramaṇa Lìyán and others.

comprising two hundred and one fascicles,

The above is one work in ten fascicles, the Vinaya Commentary (Vinaya-śāstra), Volume Two.
The *Mahāyāna-tattvārtha-ṣaṭpāramitā-sūtra-śāstra* in ten fascicles was compiled by the virtuous monk and Great Translator of the Ximing Monastery, Śramaṇa Liangxiu, and others, by imperial decree.
The above is one work in ten fascicles, the third volume of the *Sūtra Commentary*.

Furthermore, there is the *Commentary on the Mahāyāna-ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā-ṣaṭpāramitā-sūtra* in ten fascicles; these were compiled by the Imperially Honored Great Virtuous One and Śramaṇa Chaowu of Liquan Temple and others, in accordance with the Imperial Edict.

we now request that it be entered into the catalog.

Divided into the seventh and eighth fascicles.

*The Newly Translated Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, forty fascicles; translated by the Śramaṇa Prajñā of Kaśmīra by imperial decree. This work consists of one section, forty fascicles, four fascicles [in volume], and six hundred twelve sheets.
Translated in the twelfth year of the Zhenyuan era;
presented in the fourteenth year.
Not included here [in this collection]. Together with the previous translations by Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā, [the total is as follows].
A total of seventy fascicles, collected from the Great Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era; together with the preceding, they comprise twenty-three bundles.
Submitted by the śramaṇa Yuánzhào.
Last year, on the Emperor’s birthday in the fourth month, I received an imperial edict in person granting permission to compile the aforementioned Buddhist Records (Shijiao lu). Since then,
I have been engaged in transcribing and collating them,
though the work has not yet been fully completed.
I have not yet had the opportunity to submit this to Your Majesty.
I humbly observe that in the eighteenth year of the Kaiyuan era, the year being Gengwu, in the west...
The śramaṇa Zhisheng of Chongfu Monastery compiled the Kaiyuan Catalogue of Buddhist Teachings in twenty fascicles.
From that time until last year,
the Jiashu year, sixty-five years have passed.
As there was no basis for including these within the Tripiṭaka or the Sūtra Collection of the Zhongjian Monastery,
and fearing that future generations might suspect them of being apocryphal due to the great passage of time,
the former sage [the Emperor] permitted their inclusion in the canon in the seventh year of the Dali era.
The formal documents were prepared as in the preceding fascicle and issued for circulation both within and outside [the capital].
Furthermore, the commentaries on the meaning of the Sūtras and Vinaya have already been composed and disseminated.
Additionally, there is the "New Collection of the Zhenyuan Era."
It comprises eighty-six fascicles.
Some contain the imperial decrees of former emperors,
while others embody the profound grace of the current sovereign, preserved as encouragement and exhortation.
Śikṣānanda has already transcribed these and completed them in three fascicles,
together with three other sūtras, such as the *Buddhanārāyaṇabalaparipṛcchā-sūtra*, totaling twelve fascicles.
We humbly hope that [you will accept them].
May the imperial succession be supported from above, so that the precious reign may endure for a vast duration.
May the blessings of the Prince and the various princes extend over ten thousand undertakings.
May the civil and military officials of the hundred ranks be entirely filial and loyal.
May the Three Jewels flourish forever, bringing peace to those afar and order to those nearby.
Should this petition reach Your Majesty’s ears and receive Your compassionate approval,
we humbly beseech you to proclaim it throughout the realm so that it may circulate widely.
I venture to intrude upon your august presence and humbly hope for your perusal.

Respectfully submitted. On the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month in the eleventh year of the Zhenguan era, the śramaṇa Yuanzhao of Ximing Monastery, who translates scriptures and presides over ordination platforms, respectfully addresses you.
